old: It started as a word for the rough outer layer of a tree, long before it meant anything you'd pull from a bottle.
Its ancestor once meant a shoe sole made from bark, on its journey through Spanish and Dutch.
It shares a Latin root with 'cortex' — both once simply meant bark or rind.
clues: This natural material may take its name from an old Spanish word for a kind of shoe sole.
Not just any bark, it is the light, springy, buoyant layer stripped from a certain oak, used for bulletin boards and floats. Its name first meant oak bark.
You pull one from a wine bottle with a screwlike tool. Its Latin source, meaning bark or rind, also gave science the word cortex.
